name: dusty packed wasteland earth ground, a seamless 4x4-tile field with soft clumped earth with raised clods, gentle lighter dry and darker damp areas and small grit clusters running across tile borders, mixed with tiles of shallow damp hollows
label: wasteland_ruins/dirt-b

answer.evidence: The image is a seamless 96x80 field of earth texture that fills the whole frame (width 96 on every row). It has no silhouette, no standing object, no front face, no edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse. The light and dark patches (clods, damp hollows, grit) are surface texture seen from above, so this is flat terrain. That fits the caller's kind (terrain tiles). With no front face of 3 or more rows, it is measured as a flat top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows about 5 visible tones per 16x16 tile (7 colours in total): a mid brown base, lighter dry patches, darker damp clods, and small grit dots. That is above the grass reference (3 visible tones) and a little below the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as both references, so the field has no large flat fills. The dark clod and hollow edges are tinted brown rather than neutral (0% near-neutral dark edge pixels), and there is no black sticker outline, so the shading reads as dark material tone. The clods are raised by value alone, and the texture runs across tile borders without an obvious repeat. The ramp is a bit tighter and less clump-detailed than Beodeul's richest tiles, which is why texture is 'some' rather than 'rich'. Next to the grass reference it would not look thinner or flatter.
